Let

\[
B=DAD,\qquad D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,d_2,d_3).
\]

Since common scaling of \(D\) scales every eigenvalue of \(B\) by the same factor, it does not affect \(\kappa\).

At a minimizing interior scaling, write \(\lambda_{\max}=M\), \(\lambda_{\min}=m\), with normalized eigenvectors \(x,y\). Varying \(\log d_i\) under the constraint \(d_1d_2d_3=\text{constant}\) gives

\[
x_i^2=y_i^2\qquad(i=1,2,3).
\]

Thus \(y_i=\pm x_i\). Since \(x\perp y\), exactly one coordinate has square \(1/2\). Checking the three possible choices gives the following candidate scaling classes and condition numbers:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{coordinate with }x_i^2=1/2 & d_1:d_2:d_3 & \kappa\\
\hline
1 & \sqrt5:2:2\sqrt2 & \dfrac{10+\sqrt{15}}4\\[6pt]
2 & \sqrt3:\sqrt7:3 & \dfrac{21+2\sqrt{21}}9\\[6pt]
3 & 2:\sqrt6:\sqrt{11} & \dfrac{22+\sqrt{110}}{22-\sqrt{110}}
\end{array}
\]

There is also the possible nonsmooth case where the minimum eigenvalue has multiplicity \(2\). Then

\[
B=mI+(M-m)uu^T,
\]

and the off-diagonal constraints force \(d_i^2\propto (1/3,1/2,1)\), giving

\[
\kappa=\frac{17}{6},
\]

which is larger than the third candidate.

For

\[
D=\operatorname{diag}(2,\sqrt6,\sqrt{11}),
\]

one computes

\[
DAD=
\begin{bmatrix}
16&2\sqrt6&2\sqrt{11}\\
2\sqrt6&18&\sqrt{66}\\
2\sqrt{11}&\sqrt{66}&22
\end{bmatrix}.
\]

Its eigenvectors may be chosen as

\[
(\sqrt2,\sqrt3,\sqrt5),\qquad
(-\sqrt2,-\sqrt3,\sqrt5),\qquad
(\sqrt3,-\sqrt2,0),
\]

with eigenvalues

\[
22+\sqrt{110},\qquad 22-\sqrt{110},\qquad 12.
\]

Since

\[
22-\sqrt{110}<12<22+\sqrt{110},
\]

the condition number is

\[
\kappa_*=\frac{22+\sqrt{110}}{22-\sqrt{110}}.
\]

Therefore the unique minimizing scaling class is

\[
d_1:d_2:d_3=2:\sqrt6:\sqrt{11}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(\frac{22+\sqrt{110}}{22-\sqrt{110}},\;2:\sqrt6:\sqrt{11}\right)}
\]
